newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission wants TV sport for all.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission wants TV sport for all.

text.p: The European Commission is all set to propose on Wednesday changing EU law to make sure everyone can see live television coverage of major sporting events like the soccer World Cup and the Olympic Games.

In a bid to avoid hindering major European television companies' efforts to compete internationally, a proposal drawn up by Culture Commissioner Marcelino Oreja limits EU action to the biggest events.

Under a proposed amendment to the EU's television without frontiers law, pay television channels like BSKYB and Canal Plus would still be able to buy exclusive rights to sports events. But the EU law would determine how they use them.

"By keeping restrictive measures to the minimum that is absolutely necessary it would avoid putting European companies at a competitive disadvantage in the global rights market," the document, made available to Reuters, says.
Last July, for example, Germany's Kirch group won a bidding battle for television rights to the 2002 and 2006 World Cup Soccer Finals.

Under the plan, drawn up in response to European Parliamentary demands for guaranteed television sport for all, television companies would have to respect national laws setting out events which must be broadcast free either uncoded or on a non-subscription channel.
At present only three EU member countries -- Britain, France and Belgium -- have such lists, but as a result of the EU move other countries could draw them up, EU officials said.

In Britain, soccer events like the FA Cup Final, the Scottish FA Cup Final and the World Cup Final are on the list along with the Derby and Grand National horse races, the Olympic Games, the Wimbledon Tennis Championships and home cricket test matches involving England.

On France's list are the Summer and Winter Olympics, the Tour de France cycle race, European Cup football matches, Five Nations rugby union matches in which the French national team takes part, and the French football cup final.
In Belgium's Flemish region a new list is drawn up every year.
The Commission has already ensured support for its plan in talks with EU member countries, EU officials said.
